data_needed: Binance USD-M perpetual BTCUSDT 1-minute klines (data.binance.vision)
Binance 5-minute metrics dumps: open interest USD, top-trader long/short ratio, global long/short account ratio, taker buy/sell volume ratio
daily derivatives panel: funding rates and long/short liquidation notionals 2022-2025
method: Rolling variance and lag-1 autocorrelation of detrended residuals on price, open interest and taker order flow before seven BTC liquidation cascades, trend-tested with Kendall-tau across 39 configurations per variable per event.
reason: The headline result (taker order-flow variance compression, p ~ 5e-6) lives entirely in Binance perpetual-futures leverage and order-flow metrics; Vintage has only spot Coinbase OHLCV, so open interest, long/short ratios and liquidation notionals are unavailable.

data_needed: China A-share daily prices, SSE 50 universe, 2015-2024 (CSMAR/Wind/Tushare class vendor)
trade-level buy/sell classification for the LSV herding measure
cross-sectional A-share returns for CSAD
method: Lattice/network agent-based model where investors form Gaussian beliefs, herd on neighbours and receive delayed information, generating momentum then reversal; empirically compared against CSAD, LSV and a Johnson S_U tail-based herding indicator.
reason: 80-85% is pure simulation with no data, and the 15-20% empirical part needs Chinese A-share panel data plus trade-level buy/sell classification for LSV, none of which Vintage covers (Yahoo has no reliable SSE 50 constituent history).

method: Theoretical construction of optimal principal-agent contracts under drift and volatility control, generalising 2BSDE and BSDE approaches via a new contract class parametrised by a function psi.
reason: Pure mathematical finance: proofs, propositions and no empirical section, numerical experiment, table or figure to reproduce.

data_needed: IMF Exchange Rates dataset, monthly period-average USD per domestic currency, 43 currencies 2002-2023
IMF Direction of Trade / International Trade in Goods, monthly bilateral goods exports FOB in USD
method: Constant-mean multi-currency AMM whose pool membership is chosen by hierarchical agglomerative clustering on FX covariance and bilateral trade weights, evaluated on realized trading cost versus vehicle-currency routing.
reason: Both inputs are IMF panel datasets (FX rates for 43 currencies and bilateral goods-export volumes); FRED carries only a handful of USD FX pairs and no bilateral trade matrix, so Table 3's ~13% / USD 2.5bn cost saving cannot be rebuilt.

data_needed: Bitcoin daily OHLC (paper uses Bitstamp 2011-2026; Coinbase BTC-USD from Dec 2014 covers the three mature halving epochs)
known halving dates / block heights at 210k, 420k, 630k, 840k (public constants)
FRED M2 for the liquidity-versus-clock comparison (Figure 8)
optional and NOT in Vintage: Coin Metrics CapMVRVCur and IssTotUSD for the MVRV and Puell indicators
reproducible_targets: Figure 1 / Table 1: mature-cycle tops at 525, 546 and 534 days after the 2016, 2020 and 2024 halvings, and bottoms at 406/364/366 days after each top
Figure 3 turn-timing null: 0 of 10,000 block-bootstrap paths reproduce the top clustering, p in the 5e-6 to 1e-3 range
Figure 2 power-law trend on log price versus log time with fitted exponent of approximately 5.6
method: Dates each cycle's top and bottom mechanically, measures the elapsed days from each halving, and tests the clustering against a block-bootstrap null; separately shows Pi Cycle (111d SMA / 2x350d SMA), Mayer (price / 200d SMA), MVRV and Puell extremes decay monotonically across epochs.
reason: The headline claim - the halving clock - is pure daily BTC price plus fixed halving dates, so Coinbase OHLCV and FRED M2 reproduce Figures 1, 2, 3, 8 and 9; only the MVRV/Puell columns of Table 3 need Coin Metrics on-chain series Vintage does not serve.

data_needed: none - fully synthetic multivariate stochastic-volatility simulation (6 assets, 6,000 windows of length 22)
method: Trains a one-layer Transformer and an MLP on returns from a simulated MSV process with known latent log-volatility, then uses ridge probes, stage-wise decodability and output-head interventions to locate the latent state inside the network.
reason: Mechanistic-interpretability study on entirely synthetic data with GPU training and no market data at all, so it exercises none of the Vintage sources and belongs outside a free-data reproduction index.

data_needed: none - simulated Merton jump-diffusion price paths under three synthetic liquidity regimes
method: Post-training valuation-adjustment layer that scores a trained deep-hedging neural policy on tracking-loss CVaR plus funding and margin add-ons under a shared KL uncertainty set.
reason: All 15 tables come from Monte Carlo on a simulated Merton jump-diffusion with hand-set friction parameters; there is no market data to source and no empirical result for Vintage to check parity against.

data_needed: none - synthetic strike/maturity grids and analytical benchmarks for Heston, Bates, rough Heston, Heston-Hull-White and G-SVJD
method: Autonomous agentic loop that generates option-pricing code from a model spec, then scores it with no-arbitrage tests, stress tests and degeneration-limit checks, feeding diagnostics back into a method repository.
reason: An LLM code-generation and validation framework run on synthetic parameter grids with no market prices; the results (Tables 5-8 category scores) are agent-run artefacts, not data-driven empirics.

data_needed: daily open-to-close returns for SPX, FTSE 100, DAX, Nikkei 225, KOSPI, Jan 2000 - Jun 2018 (Yahoo Finance ^GSPC, ^FTSE, ^GDAXI, ^N225, ^KS11 has open and close)
Bitcoin daily returns 2012-2025 (Coinbase from Dec 2014; paper uses Bitstamp)
NOT in Vintage: Oxford-Man Institute 5-minute realized variance, needed only for the QLIKE and HAR-RV benchmark
reproducible_targets: Table 2 parameter estimates and fitted stability factors ranging from 0.732 for Bitcoin to 0.905 for KOSPI
Table 4 in-sample log-likelihoods: LM-GARCH within +/-8 points of GARCH(1,1) and 13-25 points behind FIGARCH across all five indices
Figure 6 Nikkei 225 squared-return autocorrelation out to lag 200, empirical versus LM-GARCH-implied versus GARCH(1,1)-implied
method: GARCH variant where level-and-slope updates of a latent power-law kernel sit in a two-dimensional Markov state, giving state-dependent decay of past shocks and long memory; estimated by Gaussian QMLE on three parameters.
reason: Estimation, likelihood comparison and long-memory diagnostics run purely on daily returns Yahoo and Coinbase provide, so Tables 2-4 and Figure 6 are checkable; only the QLIKE/HAR-RV out-of-sample tables (5 and 6) need Oxford-Man realized variance we do not have.

data_needed: Bloomberg SPX and SPXW option quotes, 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31, 502 trading days, 4,969,256 option pairs
implied volatility curves with bid/ask spreads across 54 tenors
method: Parsimonious three-segment parametrisation of the risk-neutral distribution giving localised control of the implied-volatility curve shape, calibrated curve by curve and interpolated across the term structure.
reason: Every result is a fit to roughly a quarter-million Bloomberg SPX implied-volatility curves; option chains with quotes and spreads are a vendor dataset Vintage does not carry.
